results.title: Extension of Postponement of Effectiveness for Certain Provisions of Trichloroethylene (TCE); Regulation Under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA)

results.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Coal- and Oil-Fired Electric Utility Steam Generating Units: Final Repeal

results.title: Accidental Release Prevention Requirements: Risk Management Programs Under the Clean Air Act; Common Sense Approach to Chemical Accident Prevention

results.title: Asbestos; Reporting and Recordkeeping Requirements Under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA)
results.key_finding: This rule represents a legitimate information-gathering step under TSCA, but its reliance on self-reporting and one-time data collection delays substantive regulatory action on a known carcinogen.

results.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Primary Copper Smelting
results.key_finding: This supplemental rulemaking appears to strengthen protections by adding standards for additional hazardous pollutants (benzene, dioxins, PAH, etc.), though the excerpt lacks sufficient detail to assess whether revised provisions weaken or strengthen the original 2022 proposal.

results.title: Phasedown of Hydrofluorocarbons: Allowance Allocation Methodology for 2024 and Later Years
results.key_finding: This rule appears to be a legitimate implementation of the AIM Act's HFC phasedown mandate with standard administrative provisions, showing limited signs of regulatory capture and maintaining the core environmental protection framework.

results.title: Updates to New Chemicals Regulations Under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA); Extension of Comment Period
results.key_finding: This is a routine procedural extension of a comment period by 14 days, which alone provides insufficient evidence of regulatory capture and is standard administrative practice applicable to all stakeholders.

results.title: Rescinding the Rule on Increasing Consistency and Transparency in Considering Benefits and Costs in the Clean Air Act Rulemaking Process
results.key_finding: This rescission actually REDUCES regulatory capture by removing a Trump-era rule that imposed industry-favorable cost-benefit constraints on EPA's Clean Air Act authority, restoring the agency's ability to prioritize public health.

results.title: Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) Program: Standards for 2023-2025 and Other Changes
results.key_finding: The rule maintains the RFS program structure but shows signs of accommodation to biofuel industry through delayed provisions and withdrawal of renewable electricity RIN generation, suggesting moderate industry influence without complete capture.

results.title: National Oil and Hazardous Substances Pollution Contingency Plan; Product Schedule Listing and Authorization of Use Requirements
results.key_finding: This document is a routine technical correction fixing equation display errors in the Federal Register and contains no substantive regulatory changes that would indicate industry capture.

results.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Taconite Iron Ore Processing Amendments; Extension of Comment Period
results.key_finding: This procedural notice extending a comment period by 8 days shows minimal evidence of regulatory capture; it is a routine administrative action that provides marginally more time for all stakeholders, not a substantive weakening of environmental standards.

results.title: National Oil and Hazardous Substances Pollution Contingency Plan; Product Schedule Listing and Authorization of Use Requirements
results.key_finding: This rule appears to genuinely strengthen environmental protections for oil spill response chemicals through enhanced testing and listing requirements, though the 17-year rulemaking timeline and reliance on manufacturer-submitted testing data suggest some industry-favorable accommodations.

results.title: Federal “Good Neighbor Plan” for the 2015 Ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standards
results.key_finding: This rule appears to be a genuine protective action imposing federal requirements on states and industries that resisted compliance, with only moderate capture signals related to extended timelines for non-power plant industries.

results.title: Pesticides; Exemptions of Certain Plant-Incorporated Protectants (PIPs) Derived From Newer Technologies
results.key_finding: This rule represents a significant deregulatory shift that exempts genetically engineered plant-incorporated protectants from pre-market registration and food safety tolerance requirements, reversing two decades of regulatory policy in ways that primarily benefit biotech and chemical manufacturers.

results.title: Updates to New Chemicals Regulations Under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA)
results.key_finding: This rule appears to strengthen rather than weaken chemical oversight, particularly by eliminating exemptions for PFAS and PBT substances and requiring pre-approval before manufacturing under exemptions.

results.title: Revisions and Confidentiality Determinations for Data Elements Under the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Rule
results.key_finding: This rule appears to strengthen rather than weaken greenhouse gas reporting requirements, expanding coverage to new sectors and improving data quality, showing limited signs of regulatory capture.

results.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Taconite Iron Ore Processing Amendments
results.key_finding: This proposed rule appears to strengthen environmental protections by adding mercury emission standards and revising existing HAP standards, though the full text is needed to determine whether hydrogen chloride/fluoride revisions represent strengthening or weakening of requirements.

results.title: Notification of Submission to the Secretary of Agriculture; Pesticides; Exemptions of Certain Plant-Incorporated Protectants (PIPs) Derived From Newer Technologies; Draft Final Rule
results.key_finding: This procedural notice announces a forthcoming rule that will exempt certain genetically engineered pesticides from full EPA registration, but the substantive content is withheld, making full capture analysis impossible until the actual rule is published.

results.title: Federal Baseline Water Quality Standards for Indian Reservations
results.key_finding: This rule appears to be a genuine protective measure establishing baseline water quality standards where none existed, with minimal signs of regulatory capture and strong environmental justice components for Tribal communities.

results.title: Addressing PFAS in the Environment
results.key_finding: This ANPRM represents genuine EPA effort to expand PFAS regulation under CERCLA, though the preliminary nature of the proceeding after decades of known contamination reflects historical regulatory delay that has benefited chemical manufacturers.

results.title: Control of Air Pollution From New Motor Vehicles: Heavy-Duty Engine and Vehicle Standards; Correction
results.key_finding: This is a routine administrative correction fixing typographical errors in regulatory citations, with no substantive policy changes and no evidence of regulatory capture.

results.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Coal- and Oil-Fired Electric Utility Steam Generating Units-Revocation of the 2020 Reconsideration and Affirmation of the Appropriate and Necessary Supplemental Finding
results.key_finding: This rule represents an ANTI-capture action that reverses a prior industry-favorable deregulatory decision, restoring hazardous air pollutant protections for communities near coal and oil-fired power plants.

results.title: Control of Air Pollution From New Motor Vehicles: Heavy-Duty Engine and Vehicle Standards
results.key_finding: This rule appears to strengthen rather than weaken heavy-duty vehicle emissions standards, with genuinely more stringent requirements and extended compliance periods, showing limited signs of regulatory capture based on the excerpt provided.

results.title: Revised Definition of “Waters of the United States”
results.key_finding: This rule reflects ongoing regulatory instability in WOTUS definition driven by litigation and political shifts, though this particular 2023 iteration was designed to restore protections before being largely invalidated by the Supreme Court's Sackett decision months later.

results.title: Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) Program: Standards for 2023-2025 and Other Changes
results.key_finding: The excerpt shows standard regulatory process without clear capture evidence, though the remand reconsideration and multi-year standard-setting approach favor biofuel industry planning needs over aggressive environmental advancement.

results.title: Adoption and Submittal of State Plans for Designated Facilities: Implementing Regulations Under Clean Air Act Section 111(d)
results.key_finding: This procedural rule shows moderate industry-friendly provisions through compliance flexibility mechanisms and timeline revisions, but is counterbalanced by genuine community engagement requirements reflecting environmental justice priorities.

results.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Site Remediation
results.key_finding: This rule demonstrates the opposite of regulatory capture - EPA is closing exemption loopholes and expanding NESHAP coverage to previously exempt CERCLA and RCRA site remediation activities, strengthening public health protections.

results.title: Federal Implementation Plan for Managing Emissions From Oil and Natural Gas Sources on Indian Country Lands Within the Uintah and Ouray Indian Reservation in Utah
results.key_finding: This rule appears to be a legitimate environmental protection action closing a regulatory gap on tribal lands rather than exhibiting regulatory capture, though the multi-year delay in establishing these protections (docket opened 2015, finalized 2022) may have benefited industry.

results.title: Water Quality Standards Regulatory Revisions To Protect Tribal Reserved Rights
results.key_finding: This proposed rule appears to strengthen rather than weaken environmental protections by creating new regulatory requirements to protect tribal reserved rights, which would likely impose additional constraints on industrial dischargers rather than benefit them.

results.title: Renewable Fuel Standard Program: Canola Oil Pathways to Renewable Diesel, Jet Fuel, Naphtha, Liquefied Petroleum Gas, and Heating Oil
results.key_finding: This rule appears to be a straightforward technical expansion of approved renewable fuel pathways that maintains environmental standards rather than exhibiting classic regulatory capture patterns.

results.title: Federal Implementation Plans Under the Clean Air Act for Indian Reservations in Idaho, Oregon, and Washington; Correction
results.key_finding: This is a routine administrative correction fixing a text duplication error in a proposed rule's preamble, with no substantive regulatory changes and no signs of industry capture.

results.title: TSCA Section 8(a)(7) Reporting and Recordkeeping Requirements for Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances; Notice of Data Availability and Request for Comment
results.key_finding: This rule represents a congressionally-mandated PFAS reporting requirement where EPA has limited discretion to weaken protections, though the emphasis on economic analysis and CBI protections shows some industry influence in implementation details.

results.title: Phasedown of Hydrofluorocarbons: Allowance Allocation Methodology for 2024 and Later Years
results.key_finding: This rule appears to genuinely implement congressionally-mandated HFC phasedown requirements with limited evidence of regulatory capture in the provided excerpt, though the industry categorization as 'fossil fuel industry' is a mismatch—HFC producers (refrigerant/chemical industry) are the regulated parties.

results.title: Proposed Finding That Lead Emissions From Aircraft Engines That Operate on Leaded Fuel Cause or Contribute to Air Pollution That May Reasonably Be Anticipated To Endanger Public Health and Welfare
results.key_finding: This rule excerpt shows minimal capture signals and represents a genuine public health-protective action initiating regulation of leaded aviation fuel, though the industry identified (automotive/trucking) appears mismatched—this concerns aviation/general aviation industry.

results.title: Federal Implementation Plans Under the Clean Air Act for Indian Reservations in Idaho, Oregon, and Washington
results.key_finding: This proposed rule appears to genuinely strengthen air quality protections for tribal communities rather than exhibiting regulatory capture, as it expands coverage, adds new particulate matter controls, and updates standards that had been static since 2005.

results.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Major Sources: Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers and Process Heaters
results.key_finding: This rule represents a court-ordered reconsideration of emission standards that has extended a 20-year rulemaking process, with the use of surrogate pollutant measurements suggesting industry successfully advocated for less stringent direct monitoring requirements.

results.title: Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) Program: Alternative RIN Retirement Schedule for Small Refineries
results.key_finding: EPA grants small refineries a 3+ year compliance extension for renewable fuel obligations, effectively delaying environmental benefits of the RFS program while citing its own delays in processing industry exemption petitions as justification.

results.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Gasoline Distribution Technology Review and Standards of Performance for Bulk Gasoline Terminals Review
results.key_finding: This excerpt primarily announces a 30-day comment period extension, which is a minor procedural action that could indicate industry pressure but does not provide sufficient substantive content to assess whether the underlying proposed rule represents regulatory capture.

results.title: Improvements for Heavy-Duty Engine and Vehicle Test Procedures
results.key_finding: This technical rule provides industry-favorable 'flexibilities' and reverts compliance modeling to an older baseline, though it operates within the framework of existing emissions standards rather than fundamentally weakening them.

results.title: Revisions and Confidentiality Determinations for Data Elements Under the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Rule; Extension of Comment Period
results.key_finding: This procedural comment period extension is a minor delay signal, but the underlying rule's focus on 'confidentiality determinations' for GHG data warrants scrutiny for potential industry-favorable data shielding provisions.

results.title: Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) Program: RFS Annual Rules
results.key_finding: EPA exercised statutory waiver authority to reduce congressionally-mandated biofuel volume targets, retroactively modifying requirements in ways that benefit petroleum refiners while potentially undermining renewable fuel production incentives.

results.title: Revisions and Confidentiality Determinations for Data Elements Under the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Rule
results.key_finding: This proposed rule appears to be a legitimate technical improvement to greenhouse gas reporting requirements rather than a captured rollback, though confidentiality provisions and flexibility language warrant monitoring for potential weakening during final rulemaking.

results.title: Protection of Stratospheric Ozone: Standards Related to the Manufacture of Class II Ozone-Depleting Substances for Feedstock; Withdrawal of Proposed Rule
results.key_finding: EPA's complete withdrawal of proposed HFC-23 emission control requirements represents a significant regulatory retreat that benefits HCFC-22 manufacturers by eliminating anticipated compliance obligations for controlling a potent greenhouse gas byproduct.

results.title: Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) Program: Alternative RIN Retirement Schedule for Small Refineries
results.key_finding: This rule provides petroleum refineries significant compliance relief by extending deadlines for renewable fuel obligations from 2020 into 2022, effectively delaying environmental requirements after industry sought exemptions.

results.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Gasoline Distribution Technology Review and Standards of Performance for Bulk Gasoline Terminals Review
results.key_finding: This proposed rule appears to be a genuine strengthening of emission standards with significant projected pollution reductions, particularly by addressing startup/shutdown/malfunction emissions loopholes, showing limited signs of regulatory capture.

results.title: Clean Water Act Section 401 Water Quality Certification Improvement Rule
results.key_finding: This rule appears to be reversing a potentially captured 2020 Trump-era rule rather than exhibiting capture itself, aiming to restore state certification authority and align with original CWA environmental protection goals.

results.title: Protection of Stratospheric Ozone: Listing of Substitutes Under the Significant New Alternatives Policy Program; Withdrawal of Proposed Rule
results.key_finding: The withdrawal creates regulatory ambiguity that could benefit either incumbent industries using existing substances or newer competitors depending on market dynamics, but the lack of detailed justification in the excerpt makes definitive capture assessment difficult.

results.title: Clean Water Act Hazardous Substance Worst Case Discharge Planning Regulations; Extension of Comment Period
results.key_finding: This is a routine procedural extension of a comment period that, while slightly delaying new protective regulations, is a standard administrative practice and does not by itself indicate significant regulatory capture.

results.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Mercury Cell Chlor-Alkali Plants Residual Risk and Technology Review
results.key_finding: This rule represents a genuine strengthening of environmental protection by mandating complete elimination of mercury emissions and adding new chlorine regulations, with only modest capture signals in the form of a three-year compliance timeline.

results.title: Asbestos; Reporting and Recordkeeping Requirements Under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA)
results.key_finding: This is a modest data-gathering rule that relies on industry self-reporting but includes meaningful provisions covering asbestos impurities and mixtures; it represents a preliminary step rather than robust regulation of a known carcinogen.

results.title: Protection of Stratospheric Ozone: Listing of HFO-1234yf Under the Significant New Alternatives Policy Program for Motor Vehicle Air Conditioning in Nonroad Vehicles and Servicing Fittings for Small Refrigerant Cans
results.key_finding: This rule appears to be a legitimate environmental protection measure facilitating transition to lower-GWP refrigerants, though reliance on industry-developed SAE standards rather than EPA-developed standards represents moderate industry influence over technical compliance requirements.

results.title: Renewable Fuel Standard Program: Canola Oil Pathways to Renewable Diesel, Jet Fuel, Naphtha, Liquefied Petroleum Gas and Heating Oil
results.key_finding: This rule appears to be a routine pathway approval under the existing RFS framework rather than a captured regulatory action, as it maintains statutory GHG thresholds while expanding market opportunities for renewable fuel producers.

results.title: Pesticide Product Performance Data Requirements for Products Claiming Efficacy Against Certain Invertebrate Pests
results.key_finding: This rule appears to strengthen rather than weaken regulatory oversight by codifying efficacy data requirements, ensuring pesticides claiming to control dangerous invertebrate pests must demonstrate they actually work before registration.

results.title: Federal Implementation Plan Addressing Regional Ozone Transport for the 2015 Ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standard
results.key_finding: This rule represents a genuine EPA enforcement action under the Clean Air Act's good neighbor provision, with modest industry-friendly elements like emissions trading and staggered compliance timelines that are standard regulatory features rather than clear capture indicators.

results.title: Control of Air Pollution From New Motor Vehicles: Heavy-Duty Engine and Vehicle Standards
results.key_finding: This proposed rule appears to genuinely strengthen heavy-duty vehicle emissions standards with extended useful life and warranty requirements, showing limited signs of regulatory capture despite some industry-favorable lead time provisions.

results.title: Clean Water Act Hazardous Substance Worst Case Discharge Planning Regulations
results.key_finding: The rule excerpt shows EPA implementing a long-delayed statutory mandate for hazardous substance discharge planning, with the limited text available suggesting genuine environmental protection rather than significant industry capture.

results.title: Regulation of Persistent, Bioaccumulative, and Toxic Chemicals Under TSCA Section 6(h); Phenol, Isopropylated Phosphate (3:1); Further Compliance Date Extension
results.key_finding: This rule represents a repeated compliance deadline extension for a known toxic chemical, following a pattern of delays that prioritizes industry adjustment timelines over the prompt protection of public health from persistent, bioaccumulative toxicants.

results.title: Notification of Submission to the Secretary of Agriculture; Pesticide Product Performance Data Requirements for Products Claiming Efficacy Against Certain Invertebrate Pests
results.key_finding: This document is merely a procedural notification of USDA consultation required by FIFRA and contains no substantive rule text to evaluate for regulatory capture signals.

results.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Primary Copper Smelting Residual Risk and Technology Review and Primary Copper Smelting Area Source Technology Review; Extension of Comment Period
results.key_finding: This is a procedural comment period extension rather than a substantive rule, making it difficult to assess capture; while extensions can benefit industry by delaying regulations, this one also explicitly serves Tribal consultation needs.

results.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Coal- and Oil-Fired Electric Utility Steam Generating Units-Revocation of the 2020 Reconsideration, and Affirmation of the Appropriate and Necessary Supplemental Finding; Notice of Proposed Rulemaking
results.key_finding: This proposed rule represents ANTI-capture action - EPA is reversing a Trump-era industry-favorable weakening of mercury and air toxics standards for power plants, restoring stronger public health protections.
